_readme: Configuration for index.html. Edit this file freely: index.html itself never needs to change for these things.
players: one entry per player. handle = exact Lichess username, name = how the player appears in WhatsApp messages. The number of games per round is half the number of players.
defaults: starting values for days per move, days a link stays valid, rated or not, and extra Lichess rules. Values changed in the page's Settings are saved in the phone's browser and win over these.

messageTemplates: the message posted when a round is created, in four parts separated by a blank line. Placeholders for all parts: {round} {days} {expiry} {type} {bye}. In 'game' also {n} {white} {black} {url}. 'bye' is only shown when someone sits out. Text edited in the page's Settings wins over these; 'Reset message text' goes back to this file.
challengeName: the name Lichess shows on the challenge page.
numberEmojis: used for {n}, one per game.

statusPhrases: the weekly status message. One phrase per list is picked at random for each game (the same phrase is not repeated inside one message until the list runs out). Placeholders: header {round}; footer {finished} {ongoing} {pending}; win {winner} {loser} {result} {details} {moves} {how} {color} {opening} {openingNote}; draw {result} {details} {moves} {how} {opening} {openingNote}; highlight {longest} {shortest} (shown only when at least two games are finished and their lengths differ; this list is optional). {details} is ready-made, e.g. 'col nero per abbandono in 34 mosse'; {openingNote} is 'Apertura: ...' and disappears when Lichess does not know the opening (it is the English name from Lichess). ongoing also has {move} and {turn}, but they are NOT reliable: Lichess hides the latest moves of games in progress, so they can lag behind the real game. Avoid them.
Keys starting with an underscore (like this one) are ignored. JSON does not allow comments or trailing commas.
